references.text: Joseph's brothers dip his robe in goat's blood and send it to their father to trick him into believing that Joseph is dead
The brothers plan to say 'a wild animal has eaten him' (חיה רעה אכלתהו) – exactly the words Jacob uses in verse 33
Jacob repeats the words 'he has been torn apart' (טָרֹף טֹרָף) when he tells of losing Joseph
Tamar asks Judah to 'recognize' (הַכֶּר־נָא) certain items – the same verb Jacob uses when he recognizes the robe, an ironic literary parallel
Jacob's deep grief because he believes Joseph has been torn apart by a wild animal
The same fatherly pain and experience of losing sons connects Jacob's reaction in 37:33 with his later lament in 42:36.
A direct narrative contrast where Jacob's belief that Joseph is dead (37:33) is overturned by the news that he is alive (45:28).
The event of tearing off the robe (9) is the direct cause of Jacob's recognition and conclusion in 37:33.
